generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: CRITICAL BIFROST AI GATEWAY FLAW LETS ATTACKERS RUN COMMANDS WITHOUT CREDENTIALS
Summary: Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway for 20+ LLM providers, ships with management auth disabled by default, so a single unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client can register a stdio MCP client and run arbitrary commands as the gateway user (CVE-2026-90898, CVSS 9.8). That exposes every stored provider API key. The official Docker image binds the management API to 0.0.0.0, and v2.0.0 only fixed a related plugin-loading flaw (CVE-2026-86242, CVSS 8.1). Upgrade to transports/v2.1.0 or set governance.auth_config.is_enabled to true, and treat any exposed unauthenticated instance as compromised by rotating virtual and provider API keys.

Editorial idea:
A critical AI gateway flaw turns an exposed management interface into a direct path to command execution and stolen provider credentials.

Central subject:
An unauthenticated AI gateway management endpoint

Visual relationship:
The gateway is presented as an unlocked service entrance: a single outside request crosses the threshold, reaches the gateway's command-running interior, and exposes keys belonging to multiple AI providers.

Composition:
Show a restrained architectural cutaway of a service entrance connected to a compact control room. A small incoming request passes through an open access point into the control room, where several unlabeled credential cards are visibly exposed. Keep the causal path clear without depicting software screens or interface text.

Permitted literal elements:
an open service entrance
one incoming request token
a compact control room
exposed credential cards
a command terminal inside the gateway
a boundary separating the public exterior from the gateway interior

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not portray the flaw as a generic cyberattack without showing the unauthenticated entry point.
Do not imply that provider credentials were merely at risk; the report says stored keys are exposed.
Do not depict unsupported physical damage or a human attacker.
Do not add brand marks, labels, interface text, or extra security products.

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
